benefits: Fixes messy exports from Excel, banks and CRMs in seconds, without opening a spreadsheet app.
Delimiter auto-detection handles comma, semicolon, tab and pipe files with one click.
Everything runs locally, so sensitive business data is never sent anywhere.
Converts between delimiter styles, handy when moving data between regions that use different separators.

faqs.a: Choose the input delimiter manually from the dropdown. Auto-detect scores comma, semicolon, tab and pipe by consistency across the first lines; unusual files can fool it, so manual selection is the reliable fallback.
faqs.q: Auto-detect picked the wrong delimiter. What now?

faqs.a: The parser follows the standard quoting rules: fields wrapped in double quotes may contain delimiters, line breaks and escaped quotes (""). It also tolerates missing closing quotes by treating the rest as one field.
faqs.q: Does it handle quoted fields with commas or line breaks inside?

faqs.a: Trimming removes spaces and tabs from the start and end of each field. Turn it off if your data intentionally contains leading or trailing spaces, for example fixed-width codes.
faqs.q: Will trimming spaces damage my data?

faqs.a: Yes. Rows are padded with empty cells so every row has the same column count, which is what spreadsheet apps and databases expect.
faqs.q: Can it fix rows with missing columns?

faqs.a: It keeps them. Fields that need quotes because they contain the delimiter, quotes or line breaks are always quoted, even with minimal quoting selected.
faqs.q: Does it remove quotes from fields that need them?

Check the live preview table to confirm the data looks right.
